name: Criora climate risk
author: Criora
description: Climate and disaster risk for any place or property: floods, heat waves, storms and hurricanes, wildfires, earthquakes, sea level rise, 7-day weather risk and country risk for 194 countries, with an interactive map. Free, no API key.

tools.name: show_risk_map
tools.title: Interactive climate risk and weather map
tools.description:
Shows an interactive map of a place in clients that render apps, such as Claude and ChatGPT: this week's forecast risk over the area, hazard events nearby as markers, and the risk by day, which the reader can pan, zoom and open full screen. Instead of the risk, the map can lay the precipitation, temperature or wind forecast under the events (`layer`), hour by hour over the week, and the reader can switch between all four. A client without apps gets the same summary as text, with a link to the place on Criora's own map.

Use it when the user wants to see the place, the week's risk or the hazards around it on a map, or when a map makes an answer clearer than a list. The figures come from the same sources as get_forecast and get_hazards_near, which give them in full.

Give latitude and longitude, or place, which costs a lookup in the shared geocoder. With both, the coordinates are used and place only names the map, at no lookup: pass the name the user knows the place by, or the map is titled by its coordinates and country.

latitude.title: Latitude

longitude.description: Longitude of the place asked about, in degrees, WGS84. Give it with latitude, or give place instead
longitude.title: Longitude

place.title: Place

focus.description: What the map shows: this week's forecast risk, the hazard events nearby, or both
focus.title: Focus

layer.description: The forecast field the map opens on, under the hazard events: the risk (default), or the precipitation, temperature or wind forecast when the question is about the weather itself. The reader can switch between them on the map
layer.title: Layer

tools.name: find_place
tools.title: Find a place
tools.description:
Candidate coordinates for a place name or address, best match first, each with its full name and kind (city, state, road and so on).

Call it when a name is ambiguous (several Springfields) and the right candidate must be chosen, or when one place is the subject of several calls and its coordinates should be looked up once. The other place tools take a name themselves and use its best match, so a single question about an unambiguous place needs no find_place first.

It queries OpenStreetMap Nominatim (ODbL) through Criora's geocoder, which every user shares and which sends one request a second: a burst of calls waits its turn, and a name looked up in the last week is answered from a cache. A name that matches nothing returns an empty list. A city resolves to its centre as OpenStreetMap maps it.

query.description: A place name or address, in any language
query.title: Query

tools.name: get_forecast
tools.title: 7-day weather forecast and extreme-weather risk
tools.description:
This week's weather and extreme-weather risk at a place: heat waves and cold (graded on the UTCI felt temperature), storms and wind gusts, heavy rain, snow and freezing rain, by local day, with each day's risk class from Very low to Critical and the hazard behind it.

Use it for the weather or the weather risk in the next seven days. For disasters already happening use get_hazards_near; for what a place is exposed to over years, get_climate_profile.

Returns for each day the minimum and maximum temperature, peak precipitation rate, peak wind gust and the risk with its physical reading; hourly=true adds every forecast step. Steps are hourly on the first day, then 3-hourly, then 6-hourly from the fourth day, so a day's true peak can fall between two steps; a day marked partial is cut by the forecast window. Source: Environment and Climate Change Canada GDPS model, read at its 15 km cell. Give latitude and longitude, or a place name.

tools.name: get_climate_profile
tools.title: Long-term climate risk: floods, heat, drought, sea level
tools.description:
Long-term climate risk and environmental data of a place or property, read at the point from 55 global layers: river and coastal flood depth of a 100-year flood now and in 2050 and 2080, sea level rise, extreme heat and cold days, heavy rain, drought (SPI-12, aridity, WRI drought risk), water stress, wind and storm days, warming and rainfall change to 2050 and 2080 (CMIP6), NDVI vegetation index and leaf area, wildfire burned area, soil moisture, snow, surface water, elevation, slope, land subsidence, land cover, built-up share and the Köppen climate zone.

Use it for what a place is exposed to over years, and once per place to compare places; assess_place has only the headline layers. For this week's weather use get_forecast; for events happening now, get_hazards_near.

Narrow it with categories, or with layers by id: the resource criora://layers, or fetch catalog:layers, lists every layer with its unit, years and source. Returns each layer's readings by band with its unit, year, cell size and source (ERA5, CMIP6, WRI Aqueduct, IPCC AR6, MODIS, JRC, Copernicus DEM and others). Give latitude and longitude, or a place name.

latitude.description: Latitude of the place asked about, in degrees, WGS84. Give it with longitude, or give place instead
latitude.title: Latitude

longitude.description: Longitude of the place asked about, in degrees, WGS84. Give it with latitude, or give place instead
longitude.title: Longitude

place.description: A place name or address, used only when latitude and longitude are not given. It is resolved to its best match by a geocoder shared by every user and limited to one lookup a second, so pass coordinates when you have them
place.title: Place

categories.description: Only the layers of these categories; every layer when omitted. temperature: hottest day of the year, coldest night of the year, hot days over 35 °C, summer days, tropical nights, frost nights, ice days, mean temperature with the coldest and warmest month, UTCI felt temperature (heat and cold stress), warming to 2050 and 2080 (CMIP6), change in the warmest month's maximum to 2050 and 2080, change in the coldest month's minimum to 2050 and 2080; precipitation: heavy-rain days (10 to 100 mm) and the wettest day, precipitation with the driest and wettest month, daily rain of the wettest month, change in annual rainfall to 2050 and 2080, change in the wettest quarter's rainfall, change in the driest quarter's rainfall, drought risk (WRI Aqueduct), SPI-12 drought index, aridity index, snow cover, snow water equivalent, snowmelt, snow albedo; wind: strongest wind gust of the year, gale, storm and hurricane-force gust days, mean wind speed, CAPE, the energy of thunderstorms; water: baseline water stress (WRI Aqueduct), water stress in 2050 and 2080 (WRI Aqueduct), soil moisture, relative humidity, vapour pressure deficit, potential evaporation, surface water occurrence from 38 years of Landsat (JRC), share of lakes, rivers and wetlands, lake or wetland type, distance to the coast; flooding: river flood depth of a 100-year flood, now and in 2050 and 2080 (WRI Aqueduct), coastal flood depth of a 100-year flood, now and in 2050 and 2080 (WRI Aqueduct), GloFAS 30-day flood forecast, sea level rise to 2050 and 2100 (IPCC AR6); vegetation: NDVI vegetation index, annual mean, minimum and maximum (MODIS satellite), leaf area index of trees and shrubs, leaf area index of grass and crops, area burned by wildfire last year (GFED, satellite), area burned by wildfire each year since 2002 (GFED, satellite); terrain: elevation (Copernicus DEM), slope, terrain ruggedness, probability of land subsidence over 1 cm a year, land subsidence rate class; landcover: land cover class (MODIS satellite), built-up share of the land (JRC GHSL, Sentinel-2 and Landsat); misc: Köppen climate zone, now and in 2050 and 2080, solar radiation, solar radiation of the sunniest month, surface runoff
categories.title: Categories

layers.description: Only these layers, by id, e.g. ndvi/annual for the NDVI vegetation index or flood_riverine/inundation for river flood depth; every id with what it measures is in the resource criora://layers. Combined with categories, both are given
layers.title: Layers

tools.name: get_hazards_near
tools.title: Natural disasters happening near a place
tools.description:
Natural disasters and hazards happening now or recently near a place: wildfires (NASA FIRMS satellite fire detections), earthquakes, floods, tropical cyclones (hurricanes and typhoons), volcanic eruptions and droughts (GDACS), US National Weather Service flood, tropical cyclone and fire warnings, and air quality (OpenAQ reference monitors).

Use it for what is happening there now. For the weather forecast use get_forecast; for long-term exposure, get_climate_profile.

Returns the most severe and most recent events first, each with its type, severity (low to critical), distance, bearing and time, and total and counts_by_type cover every event found. radius_km (1 to 500), event_types and days (1 to 30) narrow the search; without radius_km every type is searched at its largest distance, which radius_used_km reports. Give latitude and longitude, or a place name.

tools.name: get_country_profile
tools.title: Country climate and disaster risk profile
tools.description:
Climate and disaster risk of one country, of 194, for ESG, investment, insurance and humanitarian screening: the overall risk score (0 to 100, higher is riskier), class and world rank, and the climate, nature, social, governance and adaptation scores and classes, with its region and income group.

Use it for one country in depth. For named countries side by side use compare_countries; for the countries most or least at risk, rank_countries; for a place inside a country, assess_place.

include_indicators=true adds the indicators behind each dimension from the INFORM Risk Index, ND-GAIN and the World Bank (flood, earthquake and drought risk, water stress, food security, health, governance and about 150 more), those furthest from the world median first, each with its value, year, source and the medians of the world, region, subregion and income group; indicators_limit caps them per dimension, and criora://indicators lists them all. The country is an ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code or its English name; an unknown one is refused with the expected form.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code (e.g. BGD) or English country name
country.title: Country

include_indicators.description: Add the underlying indicators, the furthest from the world median first, each with its world and regional medians; the scores alone when false
include_indicators.title: Include Indicators

indicators_limit.title: Indicators Limit

tools.name: compare_countries
tools.title: Compare countries' climate and disaster risk
tools.description:
Climate and disaster risk of two to ten named countries side by side: each one's overall risk score and class, its climate, nature, social, governance and adaptation scores, and its world rank by overall risk.

Use it when the countries are known in advance. To find the countries most or least at risk use rank_countries; for one country's indicators, get_country_profile.

Countries are ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes or English names; an unknown one is refused with the expected form. Scores run 0 to 100, higher is riskier, and rank 1 is the highest risk among 194 countries. Sources: INFORM Risk Index, ND-GAIN and the World Bank.

countries.description: ISO3 codes or English names of 2 to 10 countries
countries.title: Countries

annotations.title: Compare countries' climate and disaster risk

tools.name: rank_countries
tools.title: Rank countries by climate and disaster risk
tools.description:
The countries most or least at climate and disaster risk, overall or on one dimension (climate, nature, social, governance, adaptation), each with its score, risk class and rank, optionally only those in a region, subregion or income group.

Answers "which countries are most exposed to climate risk", "the riskiest countries in Southern Asia" or "low-income countries with the lowest adaptation score". For countries named in advance use compare_countries; for one country in depth, get_country_profile.

Regions, subregions and income groups are named as the countries' meta names them; a name no country has is refused with the names there are. The filters combine, and a combination that matches nothing returns an empty list; limit cuts the list, while matched counts every country that passed the filters. Scores run 0 to 100, higher is riskier. A country's rank is among all 194 countries, 1 being the highest risk: a filter narrows the list but not the rank. Countries without a score on the dimension are counted in no_score.

region.title: Region

subregion.description: Only countries in this UN M49 subregion, e.g. Southern Asia
subregion.title: Subregion

income_group.description: Only countries in this World Bank income group, e.g. Low income
income_group.title: Income Group

order.description: Most at risk first, or least at risk first
order.title: Order

tools.name: assess_place
tools.title: Climate and disaster risk of a place
tools.description:
Climate and disaster risk overview of one place or property in a single answer: this week's forecast risk by day, natural hazards happening nearby, the headline long-term exposures (heat, river and coastal flooding, sea level rise, water stress, drought, heavy rain, wildfire, climate zone) and the risk profile of the country it lies in.

Use it first for an open question about one place ("is it safe there", "what are the risks", "should I worry about floods or heat"). For one specific question call the matching tool, which answers it in full: get_forecast, get_hazards_near, get_climate_profile or get_country_profile. To compare places, call get_climate_profile once per place.

Give latitude and longitude, or a place name, which is resolved to its best match and reported back. Returns the forecast days, the hazard events, the headline climate layers with their sources, the country summary and criora_url, the place on the Criora map.

tools.name: search
tools.title: Search Criora
tools.description:
Find Criora's documents on a subject, to read and cite with fetch: a country's climate and disaster risk profile, a place's risk report, the pages on Criora's methodology and data sources, and the data catalogue (every climate layer with satellite data such as NDVI, and the country indicators). Each result has the id fetch reads and the Criora page to cite.

Use it to find what Criora has before reading it with fetch. For an answer in one call the specific tools are shorter: assess_place for a place, get_country_profile for a country, rank_countries for the countries most at risk.

A country is found by its ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 or alpha-2 code or its English name. The words methodology or sources find those pages; layers, catalogue, satellite, NDVI or indicators find the data catalogue. Only when nothing else matches is the query looked up as a place name, in the geocoder every user shares; a place is found best by its name alone. Nothing found is an empty list.

query.description: A country, a place name, or a subject: methodology, data sources, or the data catalogue (layers, NDVI, satellite, indicators)
query.title: Query

tools.name: fetch
tools.title: Read a Criora document
tools.description:
One Criora document as markdown, with its title, the Criora page to cite and the sources it draws on, by an id search returned.

country:<ISO3> (country:BGD) gives the country's risk score, class and rank, each dimension with its class, and its most notable indicators against the world and regional medians. place:<latitude>,<longitude> (place:23.8103,90.4125) gives this week's forecast risk by day, the most notable hazard events nearby, the headline climate exposures and the country. page:methodology and page:sources are those pages of the site; catalog:layers lists every climate layer and catalog:indicators every country indicator.

Use it to read a document for research and cite it. The specific tools answer with every figure as data: get_country_profile, assess_place and the rest. An id of another form is refused with the forms it takes. A long text is cut at a paragraph, with the page that has the rest.

id.description: An id search returned: country:<ISO3>, place:<latitude>,<longitude>, page:<name> or catalog:layers / catalog:indicators
id.title: Id

Read it to find the id for the layers argument.
